Abaye: two-thirds salt and one-third water

Abaye (via Rav Chizkiya): [salting] an egg is permitted
Rav Nachman, formerly: I would salt radish [on Shabbat]
Rav Nachman, formerly: I said, I am ruining it [so it is no improvement]
Shmuel: a radish's sharpness is good for it
Ulla: in the West they salt piles and piles [of radishes]
Rav Nachman: but I certainly dip [radish in salt]
R' Yehuda bar Chaviva: a citron, but for its outer peel, would never leave the intestines
...likewise a radish
...likewise an egg

what is the practical consequence [of Rav Dimi's statement]?
Ravin: may one wash with these waters [of the Sea of Sodom] on Shabbat?
R' Yirmeya: it is fine [to wash in the Sea of Sodom on Shabbat]
Ravin: may one close and open [the eyes in that water]? R' Yirmeya: this I did not hear; something similar I heard
one of them: wine inside the eye -- forbidden
...on [the outside of] the eye -- permitted
the other: bland saliva, even on the eye -- forbidden (and so Shmuel, 108b.11)
(proposed) Shmuel's father is the one who said: wine inside the eye forbidden, on the eye permitted
Shmuel: a person may soak his bread in wine and put it on [the outside of] his eye on Shabbat
Shmuel heard one ruling from his father and one from Levi, and we do not know which from whom
Shmuel (via Mar Ukva): one may soak eye salves on Shabbat eve and put them on his eyes on Shabbat without concern
Mar Ukva, by practice: [with the salve on] he would close and open [his eyes]
Bar Livai: all this Master Shmuel surely did not permit

Shmuel (via Mar Ukva, answering R' Yannai's request for Shmuel's salves): a drop of cold water in the morning and washing hands and feet in hot water in the evening is better than all the eye salves in the world
R' Mona in R' Yehuda's name: the same -- a drop of cold water in the morning and washing hands and feet in the evening (the baraita does not say 'in hot water') is better than all eye salves
R' Mona: a hand [that goes] to the eye -- let it be cut off

...to the mouth
...to the ear

...to the member
...to the anus
...to the barrel (gigit)
R' Mona: a hand blinds
...a hand deafens
...a hand raises a polyp
R' Natan: she is a free one, and insists until he washes his hands three times
R' Yochanan: kohl removes bat melech
...and stops tears
...and grows hair on the eyelids
R' Yosei (baraita): kohl removes bat melech
R' Yosei: ...and stops tears
R' Yosei: ...and grows hair on the eyelids
Shmuel (via Mar Ukva): leaves have no [element] of healing
Rav Yosef: coriander has no [element] of healing
Rav Sheshet: hops have no [element] of healing
Rav Yosef: coriander -- even to me it is harmful
Rav Sheshet: arugula -- even to me it is beneficial
Shmuel (via Mar Ukva): all kinds of hops are permitted
...except teruza
Rav Chisda: shirka tavya is permitted
Rav Chisda: piapuei beiei is forbidden
Ze'iri: one may put clear wine and clear water into a strainer on Shabbat without concern
evidently, since it is drunk this way [unstrained], he does nothing
here too, since it is eaten this way, he does nothing
Mar Ukva: one whose hand or foot was wounded may soak it in wine without concern
it was asked: what of vinegar?
in Rav Kahana's house they said: vinegar, no
Rava: these people of Mechoza, since they are delicate -- even wine heals them
Rav Ashi, by practice: a donkey trod on the back of his foot and he sat soaking it in vinegar [on Shabbat]
Rav Ashi, by practice (the איכא דאמרי version): he was soaking it in wine
Rav Ashi: the back of the hand and the back of the foot are different
Rav (via Rav Adda bar Mattana): the back of the hand and the back of the foot are like an internal wound
...and Shabbat is profaned for them
baraita A: one may bathe [on Shabbat] in the waters of Gerar
...in the waters of Chamatan
...in the waters of Asya
one may bathe in the waters of Tiberias (baraitot A, B and C)
baraita A: but not in the Great Sea
baraitot A and B: and not in flax-soaking water
baraitot A and B: and not in the Sea of Sodom
baraita B: one may bathe ... in the Great Sea

R' Meir: all seas are like a mikveh
as it is said: 'and the gathering [mikve] of the waters He called seas' (Gen 1:10)
R' Yehuda: the Great Sea is like a mikveh
R' Yehuda: 'seas' is said only because there are many kinds of seas in it
R' Yosei: all seas purify [even] when flowing
R' Yosei: and they are invalid for zavim
...and for lepers

baraita C: one may bathe ... in flax-soaking water

baraita C: when was this said? when he did not linger; but if he lingered -- forbidden

that [baraita A, forbidding the Great Sea] is in its bad [waters]
